decisions.reason: Although this 2023 recruitment service sits somewhat outside the firm's core maritime compliance push, it remained on the website in 2024, so sunk setup costs and a reluctance to reverse a public launch make management more likely to continue than withdraw it.

This 2023 superyacht crew recruitment service is closer to the firm's maritime capabilities and is still being advertised in 2024, so prior investment and public commitment support keeping it on the market.

The maritime education programme was only launched in 2024, already shows a growing partner network, and is presented prominently, so management would likely attribute any early weakness to ramp-up rather than abandon it.

The emissions monitoring and compliance service has its own page and reports a concrete success in meeting the FuelEU deadline for all in-scope vessels, making withdrawal unlikely given both visible commitment and positive evidence.

The emissions compliance dashboard is newly developed, integrated into the firm's PAL software, and aligned with the firm's announced compliance offering, so escalation of commitment strongly favors retaining it.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool is part of the same integrated FuelEU product set, and its recent launch and strategic fit make management likely to keep backing it rather than reverse course quickly.
